pairs.evidence: scripts/census/check-library-adherence.mjs:182 The census engine is a vendored copy of another repo (PROVENANCE.json records repo + commit + per-file hashes), but drift between the copy and its ledger only prints a dim line and never fails. A local edit to the engine therefore passes `library:check` silently, which is the 'ledger is a claim, so a gate must read the tree — on the blocking rung' failure.

techniques.evidence: scripts/census/check-library-adherence.mjs:158 The gate does read the tree (re-hashes each vendored file against portedSha), but a mismatch goes into `drifted`, never into `failures`, so the check cannot refuse anything. On top of that, the existing local divergence (the ported header: sourceSha != portedSha for engine/runner/self-test) is not recorded as a discrete patch with a reason or a removal condition.

pairs.registryProposal: vendored-fork-ledger is written for patched third-party libraries. A verbatim port between two first-party repos (same author, 'fix upstream and re-port' rule) is a common variant; the technique could state whether a header-only divergence needs its own patch artifact, or whether a hash ledger is enough as long as drift blocks.
